question: What is an acknowledgment in Florida?

options.text: A declaration by a person, before a notary, that they signed a document voluntarily
options.why: Correct. An acknowledgment is the signer's declaration before the notary that they signed voluntarily.
Wrong. A sworn statement of truth is an oath or jurat.
Wrong. Notaries don't give legal opinions.
Wrong. Attesting a photocopy is a different act.

explanation: In an acknowledgment, the signer declares to the notary that they signed the document voluntarily.

question: Florida certificates must indicate the means by which the signer appeared. What are the options?

options.why: Correct. §117.05(13) certificates must state whether the signer appeared by physical presence or online notarization.
Wrong. Phone and email are not lawful means of appearance.
Wrong. Mail and fax are not lawful means of appearance.
Wrong. Stating the means of appearance is required.

explanation: Florida certificates state whether the act was by physical presence or online notarization.

question: Which is the Florida short-form acknowledgment for an individual?

options.text: "The foregoing instrument was acknowledged before me by means of ☐ physical presence or ☐ online notarization, this ___ day of ___, (year), by (name)."
options.why: Correct. This is the §117.05(13) individual acknowledgment, which includes the means of appearance, date and name.
Wrong. 'Sworn to and subscribed' is jurat wording.

options.text: "I certify this is a true copy."
options.why: Wrong. 'True copy' language is for attested photocopies.
Wrong. 'Witnessed only' isn't a statutory form.

explanation: Florida's short-form acknowledgment includes the means of appearance, date and name.

question: Must the signer sign in front of the notary for an acknowledgment?

options.text: No, but they must appear before the notary to acknowledge the signature
options.why: Correct. The document may be signed earlier, but the signer must appear and acknowledge the signature.
Wrong. Signing in front of the notary is required for jurats, not acknowledgments.
Wrong. The rule is the same for deeds as for other documents.
Wrong. The rule is the same for wills' self-proving affidavits as for other documents.

explanation: For an acknowledgment, the document may be signed earlier but the signer must appear.

question: What must a Florida acknowledgment certificate include?

options.text: Venue, type of act, means of appearance, date, signer's name, whether personally known or ID produced, and the notary's signature, printed name and seal
options.why: Correct. §117.05(13) requires venue, type of act, means of appearance, date, signer's name, identification, and the notary's signature, printed name and seal.
Wrong. A signature alone leaves out many required elements.
Wrong. The document's contents aren't part of the certificate.
Wrong. A Social Security number is never required.

explanation: Florida certificates must include venue, act, means, date, name, identification, and the notary's signature, printed name and seal.

question: A corporate officer acknowledges a document for the company. Which Florida short form applies?

options.text: The representative-capacity form naming the officer, their title and the entity
options.why: Correct. §117.05(13) provides a representative-capacity form naming the officer, their title and the entity.
Wrong. The individual form doesn't show that the officer signed for the company.
Wrong. A jurat is a different act and doesn't show capacity.
Wrong. A certificate is required.

explanation: Florida has a representative-capacity short form naming the representative, title and entity.

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Statutory Short Forms of Acknowledgment (p. 21)

question: Does a Florida acknowledgment require an oath from the signer?

options.why: Correct. An acknowledgment is a declaration, not a sworn statement, so the signer takes no oath.
Wrong. Oaths are for jurats.
Wrong. Deeds are acknowledged without an oath.
Wrong. Credible witnesses swear; the signer doesn't.

explanation: No oath is administered to the signer for an acknowledgment.

question: A notary is asked to take an acknowledgment in lieu of an oath when an oath is required by law. What does Florida law say?

options.text: The notary may not take an acknowledgment in place of a required oath
options.why: Correct. §117.03 forbids taking an acknowledgment in place of an oath that the law requires.
Wrong. The statute prohibits the substitution.
Wrong. Consent can't override the statute.
Wrong. Affidavits by definition require an oath, so the substitution is especially improper.

explanation: A notary may not take an acknowledgment instead of an oath when an oath is required.

question: What date goes on the acknowledgment certificate?

options.why: Correct. The certificate shows the date the acknowledgment was taken.
Wrong. The document's own date may be earlier.
Wrong. Recording happens later.
Wrong. The date must be accurate.

explanation: The certificate shows the date the acknowledgment was taken.

question: Two grantors signed a deed; only one appears. The notary should:

options.text: Take only the acknowledgment of the grantor who appears
options.why: Correct. Each grantor must appear; the absent one can be acknowledged separately.
Wrong. Acknowledging the absent grantor creates a false certificate.
Wrong. The grantor who appeared can be acknowledged.
Wrong. Phone confirmation isn't appearance.

explanation: Only those who appear can be acknowledged.

question: Who completes the certificate?

options.why: Correct. The certificate is the notary's statement, so the notary completes, signs and seals it.
Wrong. The signer signs the document, not the notary's certificate.
Wrong. The clerk records documents but doesn't complete certificates.
Wrong. Lenders don't complete notarial certificates.

explanation: The notary completes, signs and seals the certificate.

question: A document has no certificate and the signer asks which to use. The notary should:

options.text: Have the signer decide; a non-attorney notary may not choose
options.why: Correct. Choosing the act is a legal decision, so the signer (or recipient) decides.
Wrong. Choosing for the signer risks the unauthorized practice of law.
Wrong. Choosing for the signer risks the unauthorized practice of law.
Wrong. The notary can proceed once the signer decides.

explanation: The signer, not a non-attorney notary, chooses the type of notarial act.
source: Fla. Stat. §117.01(4)(f); Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Prohibited Acts (p. 22)

question: A signer under pressure from a relative tells the notary they don't want to sign. The notary should:

options.why: Correct. An acknowledgment declares a voluntary signing; pressure or refusal means the notary should stop.
Wrong. Proceeding certifies a voluntary act that isn't voluntary.
Wrong. A note doesn't cure a false certificate.
Wrong. Having someone else sign would be forgery.

explanation: If the signer isn't acting voluntarily, don't proceed.
source: Fla. Stat. §117.107; Florida Governor's Notary FAQ

refs.title: Florida Governor's Notary FAQ: Can I refuse to provide notary services? (p. 1)

question: May a Florida notary take an acknowledgment from a person who doesn't understand the document due to apparent mental incapacity?

options.text: No; Florida law prohibits notarizing if the person appears mentally incapable of understanding the nature and effect of the document
options.why: Correct. §117.107 bars notarizing if the person appears mentally incapable of understanding the nature and effect of the document.
Wrong. ID proves identity, not capacity.
Wrong. Family consent can't supply the signer's understanding.
Wrong. Witnesses don't cure incapacity.

explanation: A notary may not notarize if the person appears mentally incapable of understanding the document.

question: What is the 'venue' on a Florida certificate?

options.text: State of Florida, County of ___ where the act took place
options.why: Correct. Venue is 'State of Florida, County of ___' for the county where the act took place.
Wrong. The notary's home isn't the venue.
Wrong. The property's county matters for recording, not venue.
Wrong. The signer's home county isn't the venue.

explanation: Venue shows where the notarization occurred.

question: Which documents commonly need acknowledgments in Florida?

options.text: Deeds and other instruments to be recorded
options.why: Correct. Deeds and other recordable instruments must be acknowledged under §695.03.
Wrong. Affidavits are sworn and use jurats.
Wrong. Depositions are sworn testimony.
Wrong. Diplomas aren't executed instruments.

explanation: Deeds and recordable instruments typically require acknowledgments.
